question.problem:
Consider the function $L:{R}^{2}\to R$ defined by $L(x)=(2Ax+b)^{T}(2Ax+b)$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What is ${∇}_{x}L(x)$ at $x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
We can solve this problem by applying the chain rule for gradients.

Let $y=2Ax+b.$ Then, $L(x)={y}^{T}y,$ and

$$
{∇}_{x}L={(\frac{\text{d}L}{\text{d}x})}^{T}={(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{T}\cdot {(\frac{\text{d}L}{\text{d}y})}^{T}.
$$

Now, since 

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{T}y)=2{y}^{T}\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2Ax+b)=2A,
$$

we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{x}L & ={(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{T}\cdot {(\frac{\text{d}L}{\text{d}y})}^{T} \\  & =(2A)^{T}\cdot 2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{x}L & =(2A)^{T}\cdot 2y \\  & =4\cdot {A}^{T}(2Ax+b) \\  & =4\cdot {[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]) \\  & =4\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}](2\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 8 \\ 4 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -6 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-24 \\ -68\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
